A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EqNIO and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Renamed methods and reorganized material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original EqNIO evaluations using TLIO and RONIN architectures, including cross-dataset results, ablations, gravity-sensitivity tests and covariance-consistency analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original EqNIO experiments and appendix analyses and reports revised results. The separately attributed baseline results do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: The angular-rate decomposition, scalar/vector layers, learned canonical frame, backbone processing and output transformations are retained. Training objectives and the diagonal canonical covariance remain the same. The expanded EKF appendix explicitly states that this architecture component is unmodified; revised parameter counts alone do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TLIO-based models on TLIO and Aria, and RONIN-based models on RONIN Seen/Unseen, RIDI Test/Cross Subject and OxIOD. Rotation, reflection, sequence-length and gravity-perturbation scenarios already appear in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds naive double integration, attributed to Herath et al. (2020), across the retained pedestrian benchmarks. Existing TLIO, RONIN and RIO comparators remain. RIO's B-ResNet/J-ResNet and TTT variants are renamed through the +50% data, +J and +TTT notation rather than replaced.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix A.11 describes five discrete gravity-perturbation angles; v3 Section 6 and Appendix 8.11 instead specify uniformly sampled ranges, such as (-2°, 2°). This is a reported protocol revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Reported model sizes also change, while the main splits, input windows and training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: The existing gravity-sensitivity analysis is revised and receives an additional distributional view in v3 Figure 7. Several illustrated TLIO trajectory cases are omitted after matching v1 Figures 6, 11 and 12 to v3 Figures 5 and 11. The principal architecture, covariance, augmentation and sequence-length ablation questions remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds boxplots showing ATE spread and outliers for the gravity-sensitivity analysis, which v1 reports only through aggregate entries in Table 8. This adds distributional reporting for an existing analysis. Neither version specifies accuracy-experiment seed counts or confidence intervals, and the existing resource-measurement averaging statement is retained.

E6.justification: The TLIO O(2) ATE*/RTE* entries change from 2.406/0.478 to 2.382/0.479 in Tables 1, 3, 6 and 7. Table 8's gravity-augmented O(2) results change substantially: its endpoint ATE* values become 2.382 and 2.506 instead of 1.811 and 1.650, reversing the reported trend. These are revised findings under the newly described perturbation protocol, not demonstrated same-setting deterioration. Table 2 adds NDI results while retaining existing neural-method scores.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.1 adds an explicit derivation showing how an equivariant frame yields invariant canonical inputs and equivariant displacement/covariance outputs, particularly Equations 4–7. Appendix 8.4 substantially expands v1's abbreviated EKF mathematics with cloned-state and error-state definitions, covariance propagation, state augmentation and measurement Jacobians. These additions extend the formal treatment beyond notation changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain exact gravity-preserving rotation/reflection equivariance, compatibility with existing TLIO/RONIN backbones, and improved odometry generalization and accuracy. The canonical-displacement-prior terminology and Og(3) formulation reorganize the existing contribution without materially changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1 Section 7's substantive limitations concerning ground-truth-assisted gravity alignment, unexpected motions such as jerks/free falls, and transfer between hardware platforms. Gravity-estimation sensitivity is addressed elsewhere, but the unexpected-motion and hardware-transfer qualifications are not restored. This materially reduces the stated boundaries of the generalization claims.

D1.justification: Appendix 8.4 adds extensive implementation-facing EKF information, including clone states, update frequencies, orientation-error handling and measurement linearization. Appendix 8.3 revises the reported SO(2)/O(2) parameter counts from 1,821,312/2,378,368 to 8,884,870/6,020,230 without explaining the discrepancy. It also corrects the decomposed-vector magnitude description to match v1's existing square-root formula. These are documentation changes, not established architecture modifications.

R1.justification: v3 adds Leishman et al. (2014), on quadrotor and accelerometer state estimation, to the model-based related work. The positioning against approximate equivariance and the claimed novelty of handling reflections are retained. Most reference changes are citation-style or bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem setup and methodology are extensively rewritten around canonical displacement priors. The frame derivation precedes angular-rate decomposition, covariance discussion moves into Section 4.1, and experiments gain clearer dataset/baseline/metric organization. The separate limitations and social-impact sections are removed.

P2.justification: The opening illustration and architecture diagram are redrawn, and v1's separate symmetry and angular-rate illustrations are combined in v3 Figure 3. Tables receive reorganized rows, explicit units and revised captions. Trajectory montages are regrouped, boxplot axes and legends change, and Figure 7 introduces a gravity-sensitivity display. This is an extensive visual revision beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the central canonicalization argument easier to assess through Equations 4–7 and substantially improves the self-contained EKF description in Appendix 8.4. Redrawn diagrams and clearer baseline organization also improve comprehensibility. These gains are partly offset by removing concrete limitations on unexpected motions and hardware transfer, alongside unexplained parameter-count revisions. With experimental coverage and most results retained, the net improvement is limited.
